basic_information.name: Amazon Bedrock Agents (+ Amazon Bedrock AgentCore)
basic_information.creator: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
basic_information.release_date: July 2023 (Bedrock Agents preview at re:Invent 2023). Bedrock GA September 28, 2023. Multi-agent collaboration preview at re:Invent 2024, GA March 10, 2025. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore preview July 16, 2025, GA October 13, 2025. AgentCore Policy and Evaluations (preview) at re:Invent 2025 (December 2025).
basic_information.license: Proprietary (managed cloud platform). AWS open-source components: Strands Agents SDK (Apache 2.0), bedrock-agentcore-sdk-python (Apache 2.0). Cedar policy language is open source.
basic_information.current_version: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore GA (October 2025). Strands Agents SDK v1.x (Python and TypeScript). bedrock-agentcore-sdk-python available since July 2025. The platform follows AWS's continuous release model with features announced at re:Invent and through AWS What's New posts.

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: single_agent | multi_agent | orchestrator | pipeline — Amazon Bedrock Agents supports single-agent setups with action groups and knowledge bases, as well as multi-agent collaboration where a supervisor agent orchestrates specialized sub-agents. Orchestration is ReAct-based by default with chain-of-thought reasoning. Custom orchestration allows developers to define their own orchestration logic via Lambda functions. AgentCore provides a full platform layer for deployment and operations. Bedrock Flows adds pipeline-style visual workflows.
technical_architecture.underlying_models: Model-agnostic via Amazon Bedrock's foundation model catalog (nearly 100 serverless models as of late 2025). Supported model providers include: Anthropic (Claude 4.5, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3 Opus/Haiku), Amazon (Nova family — Nova 2 Lite, Nova 2 Pro, Titan), Meta (Llama), Mistral AI (Mistral Large 3, Mixtral), Cohere (Command R+), AI21 Labs (Jamba 1.5), Google, OpenAI, NVIDIA, Qwen, Stability AI, MiniMax AI, and Moonshot AI. 18 new open-weight models added at re:Invent 2025. AgentCore Runtime is model-agnostic and framework-agnostic.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: Multi-layered tool integration: (1) Action Groups — define tool APIs via OpenAPI 3.0 schemas backed by AWS Lambda functions for execution; the agent determines which action to invoke based on user input and schema descriptions. (2) Knowledge Bases — RAG over enterprise data using Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with vector stores (OpenSearch, Pinecone, etc.). (3) MCP (Model Context Protocol) — AgentCore Runtime supports deploying and connecting to MCP servers; AgentCore Gateway translates MCP requests into API/Lambda invocations. (4) Built-in tools via AgentCore — Code Interpreter (Python, JS, TypeScript sandboxed execution), Browser (web interaction), Google/Bing search integration. (5) Return Control — agent can return control to the calling application with parameters instead of executing Lambda, enabling client-side tool execution. (6) Function definitions — simplified alternative to OpenAPI schemas for defining tools.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: ReAct (default) — The default orchestration strategy uses ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) with chain-of-thought prompting. The agent iteratively: (1) interprets user input, (2) generates a rationale for the next step, (3) predicts which action group or knowledge base to invoke, (4) processes the result, and (5) repeats until task completion. Custom orchestration allows developers to override this with any planning logic via Lambda functions. Multi-agent setups use hierarchical planning with supervisor-to-sub-agent delegation. Supervisor mode and supervisor-with-routing mode provide different delegation strategies.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: First-class multi-agent collaboration (GA March 2025). Supervisor agent coordinates specialized sub-agents, each with their own action groups, knowledge bases, and guardrails. Two collaboration modes: (1) Supervisor mode — full orchestration where the supervisor plans and delegates tasks to sub-agents. (2) Supervisor with routing mode — simple requests are routed directly to the appropriate sub-agent, complex queries use full supervisor orchestration. Inline agent support enables dynamic creation of supervisor agents at runtime. AWS CloudFormation and CDK support for deploying agent networks as infrastructure-as-code. Real-world deployments include Moody's (risk analysis), financial assistants, and telecom operations.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: short_term | episodic | semantic — (1) Short-term memory: captures raw interaction data as immutable events organized by session, including conversations, system events, and state changes; directly included in the LLM's context window. (2) Long-term memory: stores structured information extracted from interactions (summaries, facts, user preferences) that persists across sessions; retrieved via semantic search. (3) Episodic memory (added re:Invent 2025): enables agents to learn and adapt from past experiences, building knowledge over time. (4) Knowledge Base integration provides semantic retrieval over enterprise documents via RAG.
memory_and_context.context_window_management: Multi-mechanism approach: (1) Short-term memory directly populates the LLM context window with current session data. (2) Long-term memory uses semantic search to retrieve relevant past facts and summaries, compressing conversation history into extractive summaries (e.g., 'During this interaction, you created a cleaning function and fixed two errors'). (3) Knowledge Base RAG retrieves relevant enterprise documents to augment context. (4) Session summaries optimize context window usage by condensing past interactions. (5) Configurable session retention from 1 to 365 days (default 30 days).
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: cloud | database | vector_store — AgentCore Memory is a fully managed AWS service with cloud-native persistence. Short-term memory stores raw events; long-term memory stores extracted facts with semantic search capability (implying vector store backing). All data encrypted at rest and in transit (AWS managed keys or customer-managed KMS keys). Session data retained up to 365 days. Knowledge Bases use vector stores (Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, Pinecone, Redis, PostgreSQL with pgvector).
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: Context is a first-class architectural concern in the Bedrock Agents platform. AgentCore Memory provides managed infrastructure for distinct context layers: short-term memory for in-session context, long-term memory for cross-session knowledge, and episodic memory for experiential learning. The system automatically extracts and maintains user facts from conversations. Knowledge Bases provide document-level semantic retrieval. Developers control what is remembered through configuration. AWS explicitly warns about prompt injection and memory poisoning risks. The separation of session-level, user-level, and document-level context enables fine-grained context engineering.

capabilities.core_capabilities: Comprehensive managed agent platform with: (1) Bedrock Agents — build and configure autonomous agents with action groups (OpenAPI + Lambda), knowledge bases (RAG), and advanced prompt templates for pre-processing, orchestration, KB response generation, and post-processing. (2) Multi-agent collaboration — supervisor agents coordinate specialized sub-agents with two routing modes. (3) AgentCore Runtime — fully managed, framework-agnostic infrastructure for deploying any AI agent (built with Strands, CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or custom code) with auto-scaling, VPC isolation, and PrivateLink. (4) AgentCore Gateway — centralized tool server providing unified interface for tool discovery and invocation, with MCP-to-API translation. (5) AgentCore Memory — managed short-term, long-term, and episodic memory services. (6) AgentCore Identity — secure agent authentication and authorization across AWS and third-party services (Slack, Zoom, Okta, Entra, Cognito). (7) AgentCore Code Interpreter — sandboxed code execution (Python, JS, TypeScript) for data analysis and visualization. (8) AgentCore Browser — cloud-based browser runtime for web interactions (form filling, data extraction, QA testing). (9) AgentCore Observability — tracing, debugging, and monitoring with CloudWatch integration. (10) AgentCore Evaluations (preview) — continuous monitoring of agent quality with built-in evaluators for correctness, helpfulness, tool selection accuracy, safety, and goal success rate. (11) AgentCore Policy (preview) — fine-grained permission control using Cedar policy language or natural language. (12) Bedrock Guardrails — content filtering that blocks up to 88% of harmful content with auditable explanations. (13) Bedrock Flows — visual workflow builder for multi-step agent pipelines. (14) Versioning and aliases for controlled agent rollouts. (15) Bidirectional streaming for voice agent use cases.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Text, code (Code Interpreter — Python, JavaScript, TypeScript), web browsing (AgentCore Browser), document retrieval (Knowledge Bases / RAG), API calls (action groups via Lambda), voice (bidirectional streaming), vision (via multimodal models like Claude and Nova).
capabilities.autonomy_level: human_in_loop | supervised | fully_autonomous — Configurable per agent and deployment. Agents can operate autonomously within guardrails. Human-in-the-loop via Return Control feature (agent returns parameters to calling application for human approval before execution). AgentCore Policy controls tool access with Cedar-based fine-grained permissions. Guardrails screen inputs and outputs. Multi-agent setups allow supervisor oversight of sub-agents. Enterprise deployments use IAM, VPC-SC, and organizational policies.
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: Extensive and growing. Native: Action Groups (custom tools via OpenAPI + Lambda), Knowledge Bases (RAG), Code Interpreter, Browser, Bedrock Guardrails. AgentCore Gateway provides centralized tool management with MCP server hosting. Search API ($25/million calls) and InvokeTool API ($5/million calls) via Gateway. Integration with AWS services ecosystem (S3, DynamoDB, SQS, etc. via Lambda). Third-party integrations: Salesforce Agentforce, Visa Intelligent Commerce, Informatica, Elastic. MCP ecosystem enables connection to any MCP-compatible tool server. Strands Agents SDK provides additional tool abstractions.

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: Yes — AgentCore Runtime natively supports deploying and running MCP servers. AgentCore Gateway translates MCP requests into API and Lambda invocations, providing seamless protocol bridging. Open-source MCP server for AgentCore announced October 2025. Agents can discover, access, and invoke tools through MCP-compatible endpoints. AWS published guidance on scaling MCP servers for enterprise workloads.
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: Partial — AWS has acknowledged the A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol and AgentCore Gateway mentions A2A alongside MCP for interoperability. However, AWS is not listed as one of Google's 50+ A2A launch partners. AWS's primary inter-agent protocol is its own multi-agent collaboration framework within Bedrock. AgentCore Gateway bridges protocols including MCP and A2A for enterprise use. [uncertain]
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: No native AGENTS.md support documented. Bedrock Agents use their own configuration mechanisms: action group definitions, OpenAPI schemas, prompt templates, and AgentCore configurations. Agent instructions are defined within the agent's system prompt configuration in the Bedrock console or via API.
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: Strong — AgentCore Runtime is explicitly framework-agnostic and model-agnostic, supporting agents built with Strands Agents, CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or any other framework. MCP support enables standardized tool sharing across frameworks. AgentCore Gateway provides protocol translation. Bedrock's model catalog supports models from 10+ providers. Open-source Strands Agents SDK can be used outside of AWS. However, the managed platform features (Memory, Identity, Gateway, Observability) are AWS-specific, creating some vendor lock-in for full-featured deployments.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: capability_based | sandbox | allow_list — Multi-layered: (1) AWS IAM controls who can create, deploy, and access agents. (2) AgentCore Policy (preview) defines fine-grained tool and data access controls using Cedar policy language or natural language; integrates with Gateway to intercept every tool call in real time. (3) AgentCore Identity manages agent authentication across AWS and third-party services with workload identity and service-linked roles. (4) VPC isolation and PrivateLink for network-level security. (5) Code Interpreter runs in sandboxed environments. (6) Bedrock Guardrails screen inputs and outputs with configurable content filters. (7) Organizational-level enforcement via Amazon Bedrock policies in AWS Organizations.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Return Control feature allows agents to return parameters to the calling application instead of executing actions, enabling human approval workflows. Multi-agent supervisor patterns allow sub-agents to escalate to supervisor agents. Guardrails can block or flag responses that fail content screening. AgentCore Policy can restrict tools requiring human approval. Custom orchestration Lambda functions can implement arbitrary escalation logic. No built-in confidence-threshold-based escalation documented — developers must implement this in custom orchestration.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Multi-strategy: (1) Knowledge Bases ground responses in enterprise documents with source citations and retrieval augmentation. (2) Bedrock Guardrails block up to 88% of harmful content with mathematically verifiable explanations at 99% accuracy. (3) Contextual grounding checks verify responses against provided context. (4) Guardrails for coding use cases (added November 2025). (5) AgentCore Evaluations monitor correctness, helpfulness, and safety metrics. (6) Chain-of-thought tracing makes reasoning transparent and debuggable. (7) Action group responses from Lambda functions provide deterministic tool outputs.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: Yes — comprehensive. AWS CloudTrail logs all Bedrock API calls. AgentCore Observability provides execution traces with spans showing reasoning process, tool selection, and execution paths. CloudWatch stores all metrics, spans, and logs. Guardrails provide auditable, mathematically verifiable explanations for validation decisions. AgentCore Evaluations continuously monitor and log agent quality metrics. VPC Flow Logs available for network-level audit.
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: pre-approval | post-review | confidence_threshold — (1) Return Control enables pre-approval by returning action parameters to the calling application before execution. (2) Bedrock Guardrails screen all inputs and outputs for post-review and blocking. (3) AgentCore Policy intercepts tool calls in real time for policy-based gating. (4) Organizational Bedrock policies enforce guardrails across all accounts. (5) AgentCore Evaluations provide continuous quality monitoring for post-deployment review. (6) Custom orchestration Lambda can implement confidence-threshold patterns. (7) Multi-agent supervisor provides oversight of sub-agent actions.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: Amazon Web Services (platform and managed services). Strands Agents SDK governed by AWS as an Apache 2.0 open-source project with community contributions from Accenture, Anthropic, Meta, PwC, Langfuse, mem0.ai, Ragas.io, and Tavily. Cedar policy language is an open-source AWS project. MCP protocol by Anthropic.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: Implements MCP (Model Context Protocol) for tool integration via AgentCore Gateway and Runtime. Uses Cedar (AWS open-source) for fine-grained policy enforcement. Supports OpenTelemetry (OTEL) for observability via AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT). AWS X-Ray and W3C trace formats for distributed tracing. OpenAPI 3.0 for action group tool definitions. AWS CloudFormation and CDK for infrastructure-as-code deployment of agent networks.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: SOC2 | HIPAA | GDPR | ISO — Amazon Bedrock is in scope for SOC 1, SOC 2, SOC 3 reports. HIPAA eligible (with BAA). GDPR and CCPA compliant. ISO 9001, ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, ISO 27701, ISO 22301, ISO 20000 certified. AgentCore is HIPAA eligible and pursuing FedRAMP compliance. VPC isolation, PrivateLink, and customer-managed KMS keys (CMEK) support data sovereignty. No specific EU AI Act compliance statement published yet, though AWS's infrastructure supports required traceability and auditability. [uncertain]

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: cloud | managed_service — Primary deployment is as a fully managed AWS service. AgentCore Runtime handles deployment, scaling, and operations automatically with no infrastructure management needed. Available in 9 AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland). VPC connectivity, PrivateLink, and CloudFormation supported. Strands Agents SDK can run locally or on any infrastructure for development and non-AWS deployments.
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: serverless | horizontal — AgentCore Runtime is fully managed and auto-scaling, handling traffic spikes without manual provisioning. Serverless architecture means idle agents incur minimal cost. Designed for enterprise-grade throughput across AWS global infrastructure. Bedrock Flows charges per node transition ($0.035/1,000 transitions). No fixed capacity provisioning required.
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: Pay-as-you-go, usage-based pricing with no upfront costs. Key cost components: (1) Foundation model inference — token-based pricing varies by model (e.g., Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Nova Lite, etc.); on-demand or provisioned throughput options. (2) Bedrock Flows — $0.035 per 1,000 node transitions. (3) AgentCore Gateway — Search API at $25/million calls, InvokeTool API at $5/million calls. (4) Knowledge Base retrieval — Amazon-rerank-v1.0 costs $1.00 per 1,000 queries. (5) AgentCore Memory, Code Interpreter, Browser — usage-based (billing started January 28, 2026). Important: a single user interaction can trigger 5-10 model calls (reasoning, retrieval, re-ranking, summarization, response), multiplying token costs. A simple agent task might cost $0.01-$0.10; complex multi-agent workflows with enterprise grounding could cost $0.50-$5.00+ per execution depending on model choice.
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: Fully managed cloud service — no user-managed hardware required. AWS account and appropriate IAM permissions needed. For local development with Strands Agents SDK: Python 3.10+ or TypeScript runtime, standard development machine. No GPU required as LLM inference runs on AWS infrastructure. Enterprise deployments require AWS Organization setup with IAM, VPC, and billing configuration.

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: Deeply integrated with AWS observability stack: (1) Amazon CloudWatch — all metrics, spans, and logs stored automatically; pre-built AgentCore Observability dashboard with trace visualizations, custom span metrics, error breakdowns. (2) AWS X-Ray — distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry support. (3) AWS CloudTrail — API-level audit logging. (4) AgentCore Evaluations — continuous quality monitoring (correctness, helpfulness, tool accuracy, safety, goal success). (5) OpenTelemetry (OTEL)-compatible format enables export to third-party tools. (6) Third-party integrations documented: Elastic Observability, Weights & Biases Weave, Langfuse (via Strands Agents community). Key metrics: session count, latency, duration, token usage, error rates.
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: Yes — comprehensive tracing via AgentCore Observability and AWS X-Ray. Traces show timeline of agent query processing as sequences of spans. Each span represents a unit of work (LLM interaction, tool execution, function call) with operation name, start/end times, and attributes. Supports AWS X-Ray format and W3C trace formats. Instrumented via AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT). Built-in visibility into agent reasoning, tool selection, and execution paths. CloudWatch console provides rich trace visualization.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: enterprise_grade — Fully managed AWS service with enterprise SLAs. AgentCore GA since October 2025 with VPC, PrivateLink, CloudFormation, and tagging support. Backed by AWS infrastructure, security, and compliance certifications (SOC 1/2/3, HIPAA, ISO). Auto-scaling serverless architecture. Used by major enterprises including Moody's, Clearwater Analytics (800 agents, 500 tools), S&P Global, Visa, PGA Tour. 9 AWS Regions. Regular feature releases with documented release notes.

adoption_and_market.github_stars: Strands Agents SDK (Python): ~5,065 stars (February 2026). bedrock-agentcore-sdk-python: ~633 stars. amazon-bedrock-agent-samples: ~780 stars. Note: the core platform is a managed cloud service; these repos represent the open-source SDK and samples ecosystem.
adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: Part of Amazon Bedrock, which is used across AWS's massive enterprise customer base. Strands Agents SDK reached 1M+ downloads by September 2025, 3,000+ GitHub stars within 4 months of May 2025 preview launch (5,065 as of Feb 2026). 80% of 600 agents in a recent AWS AI hackathon were built on the platform. Notable enterprise customers: Clearwater Analytics (800 agents, 500 tools), Moody's (risk analysis), S&P Global Market Intelligence, Visa (Intelligent Commerce), PGA Tour (automated content), Apex Fintech Solutions (financial crime investigation). AgentCore community includes partners like Informatica, Elastic, Salesforce.
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: Pay-as-you-go, usage-based. Foundation model inference is token-based (on-demand or provisioned throughput). AgentCore services (Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability) are individually priced based on usage. No upfront costs or minimum commitments. Free tier available for some Bedrock model usage. Bedrock Flows at $0.035/1,000 transitions. Enterprise volume discounts available through AWS agreements.
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: Financial services (risk analysis, financial crime investigation, financial assistants), customer service automation, knowledge management and internal Q&A (RAG), agentic commerce (Visa payment integration), content automation (PGA Tour), telecom network operations, healthcare (HIPAA-eligible workflows), supply chain and logistics optimization, software development (Code Interpreter), enterprise workflow automation (Salesforce Agentforce integration), data analysis and visualization.
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: One of the 'Big Three' cloud AI agent platforms alongside Google Vertex AI Agent Builder and Azure AI Agent Service/Foundry. Key differentiators: (1) Broadest model selection (~100 serverless models from 10+ providers) — strongest model-agnostic positioning. (2) Framework-agnostic AgentCore Runtime (supports Strands, CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex). (3) Deepest AWS ecosystem integration for existing AWS customers. (4) AgentCore provides the most comprehensive managed infrastructure layer (Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Code Interpreter, Browser, Observability, Policy, Evaluations). Weaknesses: stronger vendor lock-in for full-featured use, later to market on some agent features vs. Google (A2A protocol, ADK), no visual agent designer equivalent to Google's Agent Designer or Azure's no-code builder.

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: assistant | autonomous — Configurable. Default behavior is autonomous within configured guardrails and action groups. Return Control feature enables assistant mode where agent returns proposed actions for human approval. AgentCore Policy and Guardrails can restrict autonomy. Multi-agent supervisor patterns provide hierarchical oversight. Enterprise deployments typically use supervised/assistant patterns for sensitive operations.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Return Control is the primary handoff mechanism — the agent returns action parameters (API path, method, request body, KB query) to the calling application instead of executing the Lambda function, allowing the application to implement human review and approval workflows. Custom orchestration Lambda functions can implement arbitrary handoff logic. Multi-agent setups use supervisor-to-sub-agent delegation with the ability to route requests based on complexity. No built-in human escalation UI — handoff is implemented at the application layer.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: AgentCore Evaluations (preview) provides continuous monitoring of agent quality, comparing agent performance against expected behaviors and tracking metrics like correctness, helpfulness, and goal success rate. Results published to CloudWatch for analysis. AgentCore Memory enables agents to learn from past interactions through episodic memory and long-term fact extraction. No documented explicit thumbs-up/thumbs-down feedback mechanism — improvement relies on evaluation metrics, prompt refinement, and memory accumulation. Developers can implement custom feedback loops via action groups or application-layer integration.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Amazon Bedrock Agents is a strong choice for startups already on AWS or planning AWS-centric infrastructure. Best for: (1) Teams that want to build production agents fast without managing infrastructure — AgentCore handles deployment, scaling, memory, identity, and observability out of the box. (2) Startups needing enterprise-grade security and compliance from day one (HIPAA, SOC2, GDPR) — critical for healthtech, fintech, and enterprise SaaS. (3) Model-agnostic requirements — access to ~100 models from 10+ providers means you can switch models without platform migration. (4) Teams building on AWS who want deep ecosystem integration (Lambda, S3, DynamoDB, etc.). When to avoid: (1) If you need to avoid vendor lock-in — the managed services (Memory, Gateway, Identity) are AWS-specific. (2) If you're on a tight budget and need predictable costs — multi-step agent reasoning can trigger 5-10x model calls per interaction. (3) If you need cutting-edge open-source flexibility — CrewAI or LangGraph might offer more rapid iteration. (4) If you're building for non-AWS deployment targets. The Strands Agents SDK (Apache 2.0) is a good middle ground — use it for development portability while leveraging AgentCore for production infrastructure.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: Buy (the platform) when: you need enterprise-ready agent infrastructure fast, you're already invested in AWS, you need compliance certifications, or you want managed memory/identity/observability without building it yourself. Build (custom) when: you need maximum flexibility and portability, you're optimizing for cost at scale, or you need features not yet available in AgentCore. The Strands Agents SDK offers a hybrid approach — open-source development with optional managed deployment. For early-stage startups, the pay-as-you-go pricing with no upfront costs is favorable, but watch for cost escalation as agent complexity grows (each interaction can multiply into many model calls). Compared to Google Vertex AI Agent Builder, AWS offers broader model selection; compared to Azure AI Agent Service, AWS offers better framework-agnosticism.

confidence.cross_reference: AWS official documentation (docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock), AWS blog posts, AWS What's New announcements, TechCrunch re:Invent 2025 coverage, InfoQ multi-agent coverage, Constellation Research analysis, DEV Community tutorials, GitHub repository statistics (strands-agents/sdk-python, aws/bedrock-agentcore-sdk-python), third-party comparison analyses (Xenoss, Caylent, CloudChipr).
confidence.caveats: The platform is evolving rapidly — AgentCore GA is only from October 2025, with Policy and Evaluations still in preview (December 2025). Pricing for AgentCore services (Memory, Code Interpreter, etc.) started billing January 28, 2026 and may change. A2A protocol support level is uncertain — AWS acknowledges it but is not a listed A2A launch partner. The distinction between 'Bedrock Agents' (the original agent service) and 'AgentCore' (the newer infrastructure platform) can be confusing — they are complementary but represent different layers. Cost per interaction can be unpredictable due to multi-step reasoning amplifying model calls. EU AI Act compliance not explicitly addressed.
